acceptedWorkstreams.title: Peer-to-peer student study invite loops and instructor cohort referral mechanics
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
Turn every active student and educator into a viral acquisition engine to reach 1,000 new signups. Cohort-based learning thrives on social proof and network effects: when an instructor or learner experiences collaborative Buzz voice sessions or structured channel workflows, they naturally interact with external peers, mentors, and prospective students.

Evidence (checked on https://zedu.chat/solutions/bootcamps and /products/buzz): Zedu currently treats signups as individual transactions, lacking organic invite triggers (such as 'Invite a study partner to this channel' or 'Share your cohort showcase').

Deliver:
1. A lightweight, scalable viral invite specification mapping two high-leverage loops: (a) Student-to-student study group invite links with instant channel guest access, and (b) Instructor cohort referral links that grant extra cohort storage or workspace branding upon onboarding peer educators.
2. Micro-copy and UX wireframe flows for in-app invite triggers placed right after high-delight moments (e.g., concluding a live Buzz voice session or completing a course module).
3. A tracking and attribution plan to measure K-factor and viral referral conversion rates without non-scalable gimmicks or bloat.

Why it helps: transforms active cohort participants into an unpaid, compounding acquisition channel, driving high-intent signups directly toward the 1,000 user milestone.

Boundaries: proposed product specifications, copy, and wireframe flows only; no direct site or app code modifications, no external spamming, and no paid ad dependencies.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Three social posts a week for cohort operators, each with a tracked sign-up link
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
The accepted approach sets up sign-up tracking by source. This approach gives that tracking a steady channel to measure, aimed at the people who choose a tool for a cohort: bootcamp leads, tutors and community managers. Steps, each a finishable task:
1. Post plan (content): 12 post topics for 4 weeks, each one Zedu tip or problem shown in the live app (for example setting up a channel or starting a Buzz), mapped to LinkedIn or X.
2. Writing (content): the 12 posts in batches of three, each with a screenshot or short clip taken from the live app, one call to action and a sign-up link carrying its own tracking tag.
3. Weekly review (research): after each week, report sign-ups per post from the tracking and adjust the next batch's topics toward what converts.
No invented results or user numbers. Every product claim is checked in the live app first.
